paragraphs: Predicting solutions to physical equations from a few scattered measurements requires a model to handle changing observation locations and express uncertainty about what it cannot observe. Bias-Spectrum Neural Processes (BSNP) addresses these demands through a unified meta-learning framework. It combines architectural preferences, such as local interactions and consistent behavior under spatial translations, with explicit constraints from governing equations and boundary conditions.

The framework targets two specific failure modes. First, a model can become overly adapted to the particular points where its physical consistency is checked. BSNP resamples these evaluation points through stochastic collocation. Second, enforcing physical constraints can collapse predictive uncertainty. BSNP therefore applies those constraints to the predicted mean while preserving its learned uncertainty.

Experiments cover nonlinear Poisson equations, Burgers dynamics, and Navier-Stokes flows. The authors report superior accuracy and well-calibrated uncertainty when observations are sparse. The contribution is a way to combine different strengths of prior knowledge while addressing how physics enforcement affects both prediction quality and uncertainty.
icml-2026-bias-spectrum-neural-processes.tldr: BSNP combines architectural and physical constraints to predict PDE solutions accurately while preserving calibrated uncertainty from sparse observations.

paragraphs: Sharing information across optimization tasks can help when evaluating candidate solutions is expensive and gradients are unavailable. However, adding many weakly related tasks can spread the evaluation budget too thin and introduce harmful transfers. The paper calls this combination the Multi-Task Curse and develops MES-RET to address both causes together.

MES-RET uses rewards to guide evaluation allocation, with a stated guarantee of superior expected improvement. It also weights the transfer of search-distribution statistics, including means and covariances, by rewards. This aggregation is designed to resist harmful sharing and retain a safe fallback to independent evolution. For policy search involving different neural-network dimensions, a semantic parameter alignment strategy connects policies with heterogeneous state and action spaces.

Experiments span synthetic optimization benchmarks, engineering problems, and reinforcement learning tasks. The authors report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, including skill transfer between policies for different body structures. These findings support coordinating both where evaluations are spent and which information is transferred when many tasks share an optimization process.
icml-2026-breaking-multi-task-curse-rewa.tldr: MES-RET uses reward-weighted evaluations and information transfer to improve black-box optimization across many weakly related tasks.

paragraphs: Training data often contain both incorrect labels and unequal numbers of examples across classes. These problems interact: a correction rule that works for common classes may provide poor guidance for rare ones. CARE addresses this interaction by making the level of agreement required for label correction depend on class frequency.

The parameter-efficient framework combines three supervision sources: the observed labels, text embeddings from a vision-language model, and visual features. Its expert consensus mechanism requires stricter agreement for rare classes and allows more permissive agreement for common classes. It aggregates high-confidence predictions across these sources to filter unreliable information and recalibrate the class distribution used for correction.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, with reported performance gains of up to 3.0%. The central finding is that correction benefits from accounting for how label noise affects classes differently. CARE uses agreement among complementary signals to make this adjustment, tying its correction policy to the imbalance already present in the data.
icml-2026-care-class-adaptive-expert-con.tldr: CARE adapts agreement requirements to class frequency to improve label correction when training data are both imbalanced and noisy.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models sometimes describe objects that are absent from an image. This paper investigates the visual attention patterns associated with those errors. It identifies two forms of distraction: different attention heads focus inconsistently across image locations, and attention to image tokens fades as the model generates its response.

The authors connect these observations to an analogy with divided attention in human perception. They also provide theoretical insights linking dispersed attention to increased model complexity and poorer classification generalization. These findings motivate AFIP, an approach that enriches attention across heads and dynamically strengthens visual grounding using historical attention information.

AFIP requires no additional training. Experiments across multiple models and benchmarks support its effectiveness at reducing hallucinations through improved image perception. The result makes attention during generation a practical intervention point. The paper reports a strong association between distraction and hallucination, while its method addresses the identified spatial inconsistency and temporal fading rather than establishing that every hallucination has the same origin.
icml-2026-correcting-visual-blur-induced.tldr: AFIP reduces object hallucinations without additional training by addressing inconsistent visual attention and its fading during generation.

paragraphs: Improving language-model reasoning commonly depends on large collections of human-prepared tasks and answers. CPMöbius explores a training loop that generates its own mathematical reasoning tasks without external training data. It assigns separate, cooperative roles to a Coach that proposes instructions and a Player that learns to solve them.

The Coach targets tasks to the Player’s current capabilities and receives rewards based on changes in the Player’s performance. The Player receives rewards for solving the Coach’s tasks. This couples task generation to learning progress: the Coach is encouraged to produce increasingly instructive problems, and the Player is encouraged to improve through solving them.

The authors report substantial improvements over existing unsupervised approaches. For Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, they report average accuracy gains of +4.9 overall and +5.4 on out-of-distribution evaluations. They also report advantages over RENT on overall accuracy and R-zero on out-of-distribution accuracy. These results support cooperative task generation as a route to further reasoning improvement without supplying external data to this training process.
icml-2026-cpmobius-iterative-coachplayer.tldr: CPMöbius improves mathematical reasoning through cooperative task generation and solving without external training data.

paragraphs: Scientific problem solving requires both relevant knowledge and the ability to apply it through reasoning. A single benchmark can obscure which of these capabilities explains a model’s success or failure. This paper introduces SciReas, a collection of existing scientific reasoning benchmarks, and SciReas-Pro, a selected subset requiring more complex reasoning.

The authors pair these evaluations with KRUX, a probing framework intended to separate the roles of knowledge and reasoning. Their analysis identifies retrieving relevant knowledge from a model’s own parameters as a critical bottleneck. This points to a distinction between having learned information and successfully bringing the right information into a particular solution.

Two further findings connect the capabilities. Reasoning models consistently benefit when relevant external knowledge is supplied in context, even alongside their reasoning enhancements. Improving verbalized reasoning also helps models surface relevant knowledge. Together, the results suggest that scientific performance depends on the interaction between knowledge access and reasoning, and that evaluating these components jointly reveals patterns hidden by individual benchmarks.
icml-2026-demystifying-scientific-proble.tldr: SciReas and KRUX show that accessing relevant knowledge is a key bottleneck in scientific reasoning and interacts with reasoning improvements.

paragraphs: Physical systems often must be reconstructed or predicted from very few observations. Di-BiLPS targets this extremely sparse setting with one neural framework for both forward and inverse PDE problems. It also addresses the computational cost of producing high-resolution predictions, which can limit existing neural approaches even when their inputs are less sparse.

The framework compresses high-dimensional inputs through a variational autoencoder, represents uncertainty with latent diffusion, and uses contrastive learning to align representations. Performing its core operations in the compact latent space supports efficient inference and flexible input-output mappings. A PDE-informed denoising algorithm based on variance-preserving diffusion further improves inference efficiency.

Across multiple PDE benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art performance with observed inputs as sparse as 3%, together with substantially lower computational cost. The framework can also predict over continuous spatial and temporal domains, enabling zero-shot super-resolution. These results connect sparse-data reconstruction and efficient high-resolution prediction within the same latent-space approach, covering both directions of the PDE modeling problem.
icml-2026-di-bilps-denoising-induced-bid.tldr: Di-BiLPS uses compact latent representations and PDE-informed diffusion to solve forward and inverse problems from extremely sparse observations.

paragraphs: Locating abnormalities in rare-disease images is difficult when labeled examples are scarce and a model’s single prediction is unstable. Dynamic Decision Learning (DDL) allows a frozen large vision-language model to refine its decisions at test time. It works across both the instructions given to the model and variations of the visual input.

DDL optimizes instructions and combines predictions made under visual perturbations. This consolidation improves localization and produces a reliability score based on agreement among predictions. The score is intended to express confidence in the model’s localization, connecting the consistency of its decisions to the quality of the resulting prediction.

Evaluation includes brain-imaging benchmarks and a rare-disease dataset containing 281 pathology types, using models from 3B to 72B parameters. The authors report improvements of up to 105% in mAP@75 on rare-disease cases and performance above adaptation baselines and supervised fine-tuning. They also find stronger calibration between reliability scores and localization accuracy under severe distribution shifts and increasingly difficult tasks.
icml-2026-dynamic-decision-learning-test.tldr: DDL improves rare-disease abnormality localization by refining instructions and consolidating predictions from frozen vision-language models at test time.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models generate text through repeated denoising, allowing multiple tokens to be processed in parallel. However, repeated refinement can waste time on tokens whose final values are already settled. This paper treats decoding as a control problem, using the history of each token’s evolution to decide when further work is useful.

Temporal-Spatial Parallel Decoding uses a lightweight correctness sensor that considers confidence, entropy, momentum, and token position. It determines when a token has converged and can be fixed. Confidence Extrapolation adds a training-free state-space component that predicts future logit trends together with uncertainty. These forecasts support looking ahead and selectively stabilizing tokens whose trajectories oscillate or remain uncertain.

The authors state that combining these components reduces unnecessary denoising iterations while preserving output quality. The framework also composes with system optimizations such as KV caching. Its contribution is to use temporal evidence and position together, making decoding decisions sensitive to how individual tokens develop rather than relying solely on their current confidence.
icml-2026-efficient-diffusion-llms-via-t.tldr: TSPD and Confidence Extrapolation accelerate diffusion language-model decoding by tracking token histories and forecasting when further refinement is unnecessary.

paragraphs: Fairly dividing indivisible items becomes harder when participants’ valuations are accessible only through noisy queries. This paper studies how many queries are needed to find an envy-free allocation for two agents. Its analysis assumes Gaussian noise and bounded valuations, and relates query requirements to the number of items and the optimal allocation’s negative-envy quantity, Delta.

The authors establish upper and lower query bounds. When Delta is sufficiently large relative to m raised to the one-quarter power, where m is the number of items, the optimal query count scales as m raised to 2.5 divided by Delta squared, up to logarithmic factors. Within this regime, the result quantifies how the allocation’s negative-envy quantity affects the information needed.

The upper bound comes from queries chosen non-adaptively and a polynomial-time thresholding algorithm. The lower bound applies even to adaptive queries and unlimited computation. Thus, in the stated regime, a comparatively simple procedure reaches the optimal query scaling up to logarithmic factors despite allowing much more powerful alternatives.
icml-2026-envy-free-allocation-of-indivi.tldr: For two agents with bounded valuations and Gaussian query noise, the paper characterizes optimal envy-free allocation query complexity in a specified regime.

paragraphs: Forget gates let an attention mechanism reduce the influence of past information. Earlier efforts to add them to softmax attention used coarse scalar gates, although element-wise gates have proved more effective in linear attention. FiX introduces a way to give softmax attention this finer control despite the algebraic obstacles to a direct adaptation.

Its key observation depends on a subsequent RMSNorm layer: under that normalization, the softmax denominator becomes mathematically redundant. This permits forgetting to be expressed as element-wise multiplication of value vectors. The authors frame the resulting mechanism as positional encoding for value-output pairs, complementary to query-key positional encodings such as RoPE.

The work also addresses numerical precision, computational efficiency, and inference memory requirements. Experiments show lower training loss and improved performance on short-text commonsense benchmarks and long-context tasks. The findings support controlling retention at the level of individual value components, with the mathematical reformulation providing a route to integrate that control into a practical transformer architecture.
icml-2026-fix-introducing-fine-grained-f.tldr: FiX enables element-wise forgetting in softmax attention through a reformulation that relies on subsequent RMSNorm.

paragraphs: Sequence models need to retain information over long periods while noticing abrupt recent changes. The paper describes a tension in state space models based on HiPPO projections: uniform measures dilute recent information, while exponential measures emphasize local changes at the expense of broader context. FRACTAL introduces fractional measures into recursive memory updates to address this trade-off.

The authors derive projection operators with analytically characterized spectral properties and a tunable singularity index. This design increases sensitivity to recent perturbations while preserving spectral structure associated with scale-invariant memory dynamics. They implement it within a simplified diagonalized state space model by adjusting input projection initialization, enabling the model to capture temporal features at multiple scales.

FRACTAL achieves an average score of 87.11% on Long Range Arena, including 61.85% on ListOps, outperforming S5. These results support the proposed memory design on the evaluated sequence tasks. The contribution links a mathematically structured weighting of history to an implementation that jointly attends to recent changes and longer-term patterns.
icml-2026-fractal-state-space-model-with.tldr: FRACTAL uses fractional memory updates to improve sensitivity to recent changes while preserving structure for long-range sequence modeling.

paragraphs: A language model making decisions over a long game must compete with an opponent, adapt to changing rules, and respond to human instructions. This paper introduces a Red Alert real-time strategy benchmark designed to examine these capabilities together. Its emphasis is on diagnosing behavior across extended interactions, with winning serving as one part of the evaluation.

The interface separates the model’s decisions from their execution. Models issue budgeted, low-frequency strategic or tactical intentions, which are executed deterministically for standardized comparisons. Evaluation covers robustness to changes in rule style, competitive strength through Elo-style ratings from head-to-head matches, and steerability through standardized language interventions.

The benchmark also records economic growth and spending, combat loss ratios, and visibility coverage. These measurements provide additional evidence about long-horizon failure modes that a final win or loss can conceal. The stated contribution is a reproducible diagnostic testbed for robustness and controllability, connecting competitive outcomes to intermediate behavior and responses to human direction.
icml-2026-from-winning-to-understanding-.tldr: A Red Alert benchmark evaluates long-horizon LLM competition, rule robustness, and human steerability while logging behavior beyond wins and losses.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can predict fluid behavior directly on simulation meshes, but ordinary message passing only exchanges information between neighboring nodes. Adding connections can improve propagation. This paper first finds that connecting all nodes two graph steps apart already performs competitively with PIORF, a fluid-simulation method using long-range connections.

That observation motivates Flow Alignment Rewiring, or FLARE. It considers these same nearby two-hop connections but keeps them only when their relative direction aligns with the input flow direction. The connection rule therefore incorporates a fluid-transport principle into the graph structure, selecting local information routes according to the flow being modeled.

Numerical experiments cover flows around a cylinder, a single airfoil, and tandem airfoils under different flow conditions and with deep network architectures. FLARE significantly outperforms PIORF and several other two-hop rewiring approaches in these tests. The findings support flow-aligned local connectivity as an effective design choice, while the initial comparison questions whether distant connections are needed to achieve competitive prediction.
icml-2026-graph-rewiring-based-on-flow-a.tldr: FLARE improves graph-based fluid simulation by adding nearby connections only when they align with the input flow direction.

paragraphs: Converting an artificial neural network into a spiking neural network offers energy-efficient inference, but accumulated conversion errors create a trade-off between accuracy and latency. This paper introduces a closed-loop fine-tuning framework that corrects these errors while leaving the source network unchanged. It therefore retains the ability to start with an off-the-shelf artificial neural network.

The method aligns both outputs and internal features. Global Kullback-Leibler divergence transfers output behavior, while a local Centered Kernel Alignment constraint matches representations and is weighted using initial conversion loss. The authors find that these components matter differently across time budgets: local constraints stabilize low-latency representations, whereas global alignment drives fidelity at higher numbers of time steps.

On CIFAR-10, converted networks retain over 99% of source accuracy at 32 time steps. One ResNet-18 example reaches 96.38%, compared with the source’s 96.39%. Fine-tuning also acts as a regularizer, producing input-noise robustness that matches or exceeds the source model. The results connect representation alignment to accurate, robust conversion.
icml-2026-high-fidelity-ann-to-snn-conve.tldr: Closed-loop output and feature distillation preserves source-network accuracy in converted spiking networks while improving robustness to input noise.

paragraphs: Image generators can produce high-quality outputs yet repeatedly favor a narrow set of possibilities. This paper identifies the starting noise as a source of that limited diversity: standard Gaussian initialization ignores the guidance landscape and can send generation trajectories toward dominant modes. The authors therefore make initialization itself the target of intervention.

They formulate a guidance potential posterior that reweights the noise prior toward regions associated with greater diversity. Diversity-inducing Initialization, or DivIn, samples this distribution using Langevin dynamics. It actively moves starting noise away from regions associated with collapse while keeping it anchored to the valid data manifold. The method operates at inference time and supports both diffusion and flow matching models.

Experiments in class-conditioned and text-conditioned image generation show superior performance. DivIn can also be combined with methods that intervene along the generation trajectory. The authors report that this combination substantially expands the achievable diversity-quality frontier, supporting initialization as a complementary place to improve the range of generated images.
icml-2026-initialization-is-half-the-bat.tldr: DivIn improves image diversity by selecting starting noise using the guidance landscape and complements methods that modify generation trajectories.

paragraphs: An agent with frozen language-model weights can struggle to adapt as it gains experience. Just-In-Time Reinforcement Learning (JitRL) enables test-time policy optimization without gradient updates. It stores experience in a changing, non-parametric memory, allowing past interactions to influence future decisions without fine-tuning the underlying model.

For each decision, JitRL retrieves relevant trajectories and estimates action advantages on the fly. These estimates directly adjust the model’s output logits, changing which actions it favors. The authors prove that the additive update is the exact closed-form solution to a policy optimization objective constrained by KL divergence. This supplies a theoretical basis for the particular way experience modifies action selection.

Experiments on WebArena and Jericho establish a new state of the art among training-free methods. The authors also report outperforming expensive fine-tuning approaches, including WebRL, while reducing monetary costs by more than a factor of 30. These findings support experience-based adaptation through memory and output adjustment as a practical route to continual agent learning.
icml-2026-just-in-time-reinforcement-lea.tldr: JitRL adapts frozen LLM agents by retrieving past experience and directly adjusting action logits without gradient updates.

paragraphs: Preference training presents language models with more than one kind of difficulty. Some examples require understanding a complex prompt, while others require choosing between closely matched responses. This paper argues that treating all preference pairs uniformly overlooks these distinct demands and that their learning schedules should be controlled separately.

Gradient analysis reveals a layer-wise pattern: semantic complexity predominantly affects updates in lower layers, while uncertainty about preferences modulates upper layers. Based on this finding, the authors introduce Gradient-Guided Disentangled DPO, or GDO-DPO. Its curriculum independently regulates the pace of learning along the semantic and preference dimensions using gradient stability in the relevant layers.

Experiments on UltraFeedback and HH-RLHF show consistent improvements. GDO-DPO outperforms standard DPO by a reported 4.1% on AlpacaEval 2.0, with especially strong gains on reasoning-intensive tasks. The findings support using internal training signals to distinguish understanding difficulty from preference ambiguity, then adapting the curriculum to those different demands instead of advancing them at a single shared pace.
icml-2026-layer-wise-gradient-disentangl.tldr: GDO-DPO uses layer-specific gradient stability to separately pace learning of prompt semantics and response preferences.

paragraphs: Molecular property predictors often learn from a limited part of chemical space. When molecular scaffolds or functional compositions change, patterns that helped during training may stop being useful. MoSIR addresses this problem by separating molecular information intended to remain stable across environments from variations that are sensitive to the training environment.

The framework projects mixed molecular embeddings into a learnable space of semantic prototypes. This decomposition supports a bi-level min-max objective that perturbs representations to simulate plausible environmental changes and encourages semantic stability under those changes. The prototypes provide a structured space in which the model can distinguish transferable chemical meaning from environment-sensitive variation.

The authors derive an out-of-distribution generalization bound and evaluate MoSIR on multiple molecular benchmarks with different kinds of distribution shift. It consistently outperforms strong baselines in those experiments. Qualitative analyses also indicate that the prototypes capture meaningful chemical semantics. Together, the results support combining prototype-based separation with perturbation-based training to improve transfer beyond the chemical environments represented in training.
icml-2026-learning-molecular-semantic-in.tldr: MoSIR learns molecular prototypes and trains for semantic stability under simulated shifts to improve out-of-distribution property prediction.

paragraphs: Muon improves optimization geometry by orthogonalizing parameter updates, but this paper identifies an imbalance left by that operation. Different neurons can receive updates with very different norms, allowing some to dominate training. NorMuon combines Muon’s orthogonalization with neuron-level adaptive learning rates to address this uneven use of parameters.

The optimizer tracks second-moment statistics for each neuron and applies row-wise normalization after orthogonalization. This balances update magnitudes while preserving the conditioning benefits attributed to Muon. For larger training runs, the authors also develop an FSDP2 implementation that distributes orthogonalization computations across devices, making the combined method practical at scale.

Experiments across multiple model sizes show consistent improvements over AdamW and Muon. On 1.1B-parameter pretraining, NorMuon reduces training steps by 21.74% relative to AdamW, with an efficiency gain 11.31 percentage points larger than Muon’s. These results suggest that improved conditioning and adaptive learning rates can complement each other, with neuron-level normalization addressing an imbalance that orthogonalization alone leaves unresolved.
icml-2026-normuon-making-muon-more-effic.tldr: NorMuon combines orthogonalized updates with neuron-wise adaptive normalization to improve language-model training efficiency.

paragraphs: Language-model serving often separates prompt processing, called prefill, from token-by-token decoding. In multi-turn conversations, repeated processing and transfers of cached key-value states can cause high latency and congest the network. This paper observes that append-prefill, which processes new input while reusing cached states, disrupts decoding substantially less than full prefill.

That distinction creates an opportunity to handle later turns directly on decode nodes. However, the authors find that no single fixed routing strategy meets all service-level objectives simultaneously. Their Prefill Prefill-capable Decode architecture, or PPD, dynamically decides when to process Turn 2 and later requests locally. Configurable weights adapt routing to different service objectives, and the system integrates with existing prefill-decode deployments.

Evaluations show a 68% reduction in time to first token for later turns while maintaining competitive time per output token. PPD also alleviates cache-transfer congestion under high load. The results support treating cached continuation processing as a distinct workload whose placement should respond to service requirements.
icml-2026-not-all-prefills-are-equal-ppd.tldr: PPD dynamically routes later conversation turns to cache-holding decode nodes, reducing response latency and cache-transfer congestion.

paragraphs: When the number of variables in logistic regression grows with the sample size, common estimators have asymptotic behavior involving nonzero bias and variance factors. Those factors depend on signal strength. Accurately estimating signal strength is therefore an important step toward turning high-dimensional theory into valid statistical methods.

This paper develops an efficient estimation strategy based on splitting the data. It also addresses difficulties caused by separable data through an M-estimator with a data-driven regularizer. The regularizer is non-decomposable and adapts to the true covariance structure, making the dependence among variables part of the analysis rather than treating regularization as independent adjustments to individual coordinates.

The authors derive exact asymptotic behavior for this estimator and support the method with numerical experiments. The stated contribution is both an estimator of the signal strength needed by the theory and an analysis that accommodates the separability issue. Its significance lies in connecting a difficult underlying quantity to usable statistical methodology in the regime where dimension grows alongside sample size.
icml-2026-signal-strength-estimation-in-.tldr: A data-splitting method estimates signal strength in high-dimensional logistic regression, with theory addressing separability through covariance-adaptive regularization.

paragraphs: LLM reinforcement learning often updates a policy using sequences generated by a slightly different rollout policy. Backend differences, routing discontinuities, and stale distributed computations can create this mismatch. The paper examines how it affects the gap between the surrogate training objective and the true objective, particularly for long generated sequences.

The authors show that classical trust-region error bounds grow quadratically with sequence length, becoming uninformative for long-horizon tasks. They derive two alternatives: a Pinsker-Marginal bound growing as length to the power of 1.5 and a Mixed bound growing linearly. Both depend on the maximum token-level KL divergence anywhere in the sequence, creating a sequence-wide condition that token-independent PPO clipping cannot control.

Trust Region Masking enforces this perspective by masking entire sequences that violate the trust region. The contribution is a more informative theoretical framework and a matching training intervention for policy mismatch. It offers a principled way to mitigate long-horizon training collapse by evaluating whether each full sequence satisfies the relevant divergence condition.
icml-2026-trust-region-masking-for-long-.tldr: Trust Region Masking excludes whole sequences that violate a divergence condition, using tighter error bounds for long-horizon LLM reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Bayesian persuasion studies how a sender’s choice of information influences a receiver’s optimal behavior. Traditional formulations often express information structures numerically, making them difficult to apply to rich dialogue. This paper develops a verbalized framework that brings these information-design questions into natural-language games involving language-model senders and receivers.

The framework maps persuasion into a game augmented by a mediator and combines an LLM with a game solver to find equilibria. Its supporting techniques express commitment assumptions and obedience constraints in language and use information obfuscation. These components connect the game’s strategic requirements to interactions carried out through dialogue.

Experiments include recommendation letters, law enforcement, and diplomacy with the press. The framework reproduces theoretical results from classic Bayesian persuasion and discovers effective strategies in more complex natural-language and multi-stage scenarios. The findings support using verbal interaction as part of a game-theoretic computation, while keeping the sender’s objectives and the receiver’s response incentives central to the analysis.
icml-2026-verbalized-bayesian-persuasion.tldr: A verbalized Bayesian persuasion framework combines LLM dialogue with a game solver to study strategic information sharing in natural-language scenarios.

paragraphs: Quantization-aware training updates full-precision weights using gradients from a quantized model, but convergence can be slow, especially below four bits. This paper investigates the loss surface through Hessian spectra. It finds training settles into flat regions around saddle points, with increasingly many eigenvalues near zero and smaller eigenvalue magnitudes at lower bit widths.

WinQ responds with two modifications. It periodically moves weights to a linear interpolation between their full-precision and quantized values, reducing their distance from the quantization grid and increasing eigenvalue magnitudes. It also computes gradients using noise-injected weights to regularize the Hessian. Both changes target the geometry associated with slow progress.

Across different models and quantization methods, WinQ accelerates training by up to four times. At the same training cost, it improves state-of-the-art sub-four-bit quantization performance by up to 8.8%. Results are consistent across 16 settings. These findings support intervening in the local loss geometry as a way to improve both convergence speed and the performance attainable within a fixed training budget.
icml-2026-winq-accelerating-quantization.tldr: WinQ accelerates quantization-aware training by periodically interpolating weights toward quantized values and computing gradients with injected noise.
